plants.name: Spikemoss
plants.shortDescription: A small, green, seedless vascular plant with branching stems and tiny leaves that reproduces through spores.
plants.description: A small, green, seedless vascular plant with branching stems and tiny leaves. It reproduces through spores instead of seeds.
medicinalUses: Some species are traditionally used in herbal medicine
Studied for potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties
plants.preparation: No established medicinal preparation is recommended without proper species identification.
plants.habitat: Commonly grows in moist, shaded areas, forest floors, damp soil, and rocks.
plants.cultivation: Grows in moist, well-drained soil with high humidity and indirect sunlight.
plants.precautions: Avoid excessive sunlight and waterlogging. Do not consume or use medicinally without proper identification.
plants.funFact: Selaginella produces two types of spores: megaspores (female) and microspores (male). This is called heterospory.
plants.collectedBy: Vaneeza C. Morre, Valeery C. Morre, Jona Rose Abad

plants.name: Climbing Fern
plants.shortDescription: A climbing fern with long, slender, flexible stems and green leaves divided into smaller leaflets.
plants.description: Lygodium is a climbing fern with long, slender, and flexible stems. It has green leaves divided into smaller leaflets. It grows by climbing and wrapping around nearby plants and supports.
medicinalUses: Some species have been used in traditional medicine, but their safety and effectiveness are not well established.
plants.preparation: Clean the collected specimen gently, arrange its leaves, and press it between sheets of newspaper to preserve it.
plants.habitat: Commonly found in moist, shady areas, forests, grasslands, and places with nearby vegetation.
plants.cultivation: It grows in moist soil with partial shade and needs regular watering. It can spread through spores.
plants.precautions: Avoid damaging the plant unnecessarily. Do not eat or use it as medicine without proper identification and expert advice.
plants.funFact: Unlike most ferns, Lygodium has climbing leaf stalks that can grow very long and wrap around other plants.

plants.name: Paku-pakuan
plants.shortDescription: A green, terrestrial fern with long, creeping underground stems and divided, hairy leaves that grows in moist, shaded areas.
plants.description: Christella parasitica is a terrestrial perennial fern growing 30–100 cm tall, with long, creeping underground stems and divided leaves. Its leaves are usually light to bright green, soft-textured, and have small hairs underneath, especially along the veins. It commonly grows in moist and shaded areas.
medicinalUses: Gout & Rheumatism: Decoction of fronds/rhizome taken orally to reduce inflammation and joint pain
Wounds & Skin Conditions: Leaf poultice applied to wounds, burns, boils, and swelling; helps stop bleeding
Gastrointestinal: Leaf decoction used for dysentery, indigestion, and as an anthelmintic (expels intestinal worms)
Other: Used in traditional remedies for fever, urinary disorders, and as a general tonic
plants.preparation: Decoction: Boil 15–30g of fresh fronds or rhizome in 2 cups of water for 10–15 minutes; drink 2–3 times daily. Poultice: Crush fresh leaves into a paste; apply directly to affected areas; change 2× daily. Hair Wash: Leaf decoction used as rinse to clean hair and treat dandruff/scalp conditions.
plants.habitat: It commonly grows in tropical forests, moist and shaded places, along streams, roadsides, forest edges, and open damp areas. It is widely distributed throughout the Philippines.
plants.cultivation: It can be grown in gardens or containers. It grows well in moist, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter with partial shade and a tropical environment.
plants.precautions: There is limited information about its safety and possible risks. Not recommended for pregnant/nursing women. Avoid consuming or applying it medicinally without consulting a qualified healthcare professional.
plants.funFact: Despite the name 'parasitica,' this fern is NOT a parasite! It gets its name because early botanists often found it growing on decaying tree trunks, giving the false impression it was parasitic — but it makes its own food via photosynthesis.
plants.collectedBy: Kristy Jane V. Mondoñedo, Erich Padigos

plants.name: Tuberous sword fern (Pako)
plants.shortDescription: A perennial fern with upright or arching green fronds and small, round tubers on its underground stems.
plants.description: Nephrolepis cordifolia is a perennial fern with upright or arching green fronds. Its leaves are divided into many small, narrow leaflets arranged along a central stem. It also develops small round structures called tubers on its underground stems, which help it store nutrients and reproduce.
medicinalUses: Some traditional communities use certain fern species in herbal practices. However, the medicinal benefits and safety of Nephrolepis cordifolia are not sufficiently established.
plants.preparation: For herbarium preservation, the fronds are arranged between sheets of paper, pressed flat, and dried completely.
plants.habitat: It commonly grows in tropical and subtropical regions, including gardens, forests, grasslands, roadsides, and other areas with sufficient moisture.
plants.cultivation: It grows well in moist, well-drained soil and partial shade. Regular watering and a humid environment help maintain healthy growth. It can be cultivated in pots, gardens, and landscaped areas.
plants.precautions: Avoid eating the plant or using it as medicine without proper identification and professional guidance. It can spread through its underground tubers, so its growth should be monitored when cultivated.
plants.funFact: Nephrolepis cordifolia is called Tuberous Sword Fern because it produces small, round, potato-like tubers that store food and help the plant survive unfavorable conditions.

plants.name: Bracken Fern
plants.shortDescription: A perennial fern with creeping underground rhizomes and large, triangular fronds divided into many smaller leaflets.
plants.description: A perennial fern with creeping underground rhizomes and large, triangular fronds divided into many smaller leaflets. Mature fronds are often broadly spreading and may grow tall.
medicinalUses: Not recommended for medicinal use because the plant contains potentially harmful compounds that may be harmful to humans and animals.
plants.preparation: No home preparation is recommended because the plant contains potentially harmful compounds.
plants.habitat: Common in open woodlands, grasslands, forest edges, and disturbed areas. It grows in different soil conditions and can form large colonies.
plants.cultivation: It can grow in sunny or partly shaded places and may spread vigorously.
plants.precautions: Do not eat or prepare this fern. It contains ptaquiloside and other compounds associated with toxicity. Avoid ingestion and handle responsibly.
plants.funFact: Bracken fern is one of the most widespread ferns in the world and can grow in many different environments.

plants.name: Nito
plants.shortDescription: A perennial climbing fern with slender, twining stems and green, divided leaflets that can climb over nearby plants and trees.
plants.description: A perennial climbing fern with slender, twining stems and green, divided leaflets. It can climb over nearby plants and trees.
medicinalUses: Traditionally used in some Asian herbal practices for urinary problems, inflammation, and wound treatment. However, its medicinal effects are not fully established in humans.
plants.preparation: Traditionally prepared as a herbal decoction or paste. Not recommended for home medicinal use without professional guidance.
plants.habitat: Commonly grows in moist forests, shaded areas, woodland edges, and along streams. Native to tropical and subtropical Asia, including the Philippines.
plants.cultivation: Thrives in moist soil and partial shade; spreads through spores and rhizomes and may grow aggressively.
plants.precautions: Avoid consumption without expert advice, do not replace prescribed medicine, and control its spread.
plants.funFact: Unlike most ferns, Lygodium japonicum has climbing fronds that can twine around other plants and grow several meters long.
plants.collectedBy: Jeany Rose D. Mendez, Charice Recaña, Jellan Patriarca

plants.name: Giant Sword Fern
plants.shortDescription: A large green fern with long, narrow fronds and slightly toothed leaflets growing on both sides of the central stem.
plants.description: Nephrolepis biserrata is a large green fern with long, narrow leaves arranged along a central stem. Its leaflets have slightly toothed edges and grow on both sides of the stem. It does not produce flowers or seeds but reproduces through spores.
medicinalUses: It has been reported to have traditional medicinal uses in some countries. However, its medicinal benefits are not yet well established, and more scientific studies are needed.
plants.preparation: It is commonly grown as an ornamental plant. No established safe medicinal preparation is recommended.
plants.habitat: It commonly grows in tropical areas, especially in moist soil, forests, swamps, grasslands, and shaded places. It can also grow on tree trunks.
plants.cultivation: It can be grown by dividing its roots or runners. It grows well in moist, fertile soil with partial shade and regular watering.
plants.precautions: Avoid using the plant as medicine without proper guidance. Keep it away from areas where it may be accidentally damaged or eaten by pets.
plants.funFact: Nephrolepis biserrata is also called Giant Sword Fern because its long, sword-shaped fronds can grow up to several meters in length.
plants.collectedBy: Marianne J. Ancis, Lhyza Luardo, Sharmaine Martinez

plants.name: Brake Fern
plants.shortDescription: A tropical fern with delicate, feather-like green fronds that reproduces through spores instead of seeds or flowers.
plants.description: A tropical fern with delicate, feather-like green fronds. It reproduces through spores instead of seeds or flowers.
medicinalUses: No established medicinal uses are confirmed for this unidentified Pteris species. Mainly valued as an ornamental plant.
plants.preparation: No established medicinal preparation. Not recommended for consumption.
plants.habitat: Grows in moist and shaded environments, commonly found in forest areas, grassy places, and near rocks.
plants.cultivation: Grows best in moist soil and partially shaded area with sufficient humidity and good drainage.
plants.precautions: Avoid consuming the plant without proper identification. Protect its natural habitat and avoid unnecessary collection.
plants.funFact: Unlike flowering plants, ferns reproduce through tiny spores instead of seeds. Their beautiful divided leaves are called fronds.

plants.name: Nephrolepis
plants.shortDescription: A green fern with long, feather-like fronds, commonly grown as an ornamental plant in tropical and subtropical regions.
plants.description: Nephrolepis is a green fern with long, narrow leaves arranged in a feather-like pattern. Its leaves are called fronds and are divided into smaller leaflets. It has fibrous roots and a short underground stem called a rhizome. It grows in moist and shady areas, such as forests and gardens. It does not produce flowers or seeds but reproduces through spores. It is commonly used as an ornamental plant for decoration.
medicinalUses: Nephrolepis has no scientifically proven medicinal uses and is mainly grown as an ornamental plant.
plants.preparation: No established medicinal preparation. Not recommended for consumption.
plants.habitat: Nephrolepis grows in moist, shady, and humid environments, such as forests, gardens, and areas near streams. It commonly thrives in tropical and subtropical regions.
plants.cultivation: Nephrolepis grows in moist soil with partial shade and regular watering. It thrives in humid environments and can be propagated through spores or root division. It can also spread through runners called stolons.
plants.precautions: Nephrolepis is generally safe to touch, but avoid eating any part of the plant. Wash your hands after handling it and keep it away from children and pets.
plants.funFact: Nephrolepis is an ancient group of ferns that existed millions of years ago. It reproduces through spores instead of seeds. Its leaves are called fronds, and the tiny clusters of spores underneath them are called sori.

plants.name: Wart Fern
plants.shortDescription: A tropical fern with simple, elongated, light-green leaves and a creeping rhizome that reproduces through spores.
plants.description: A tropical fern with simple, elongated, light-green leaves. Its leaves are smooth, slightly wavy along the edges, and grow from a creeping rhizome. It does not produce flowers or seeds but reproduces through spores.
medicinalUses: No well-established medicinal uses. Mainly used as an ornamental plant.
plants.preparation: No established medicinal preparation. Not recommended for consumption.
plants.habitat: Grows in moist, shaded environments, usually on rocks and tree trunks.
plants.cultivation: Grows best in shaded areas with high humidity and moist, well-drained growing conditions.
plants.precautions: Avoid consuming or using it medicinally without verified safety information. Handle carefully and protect its natural habitat.
plants.funFact: Ferns like Microsorum punctatum can grow without soil by attaching their roots to rocks or tree trunks, allowing them to thrive in natural forest environments.

plants.name: Serrated Fern
plants.shortDescription: A perennial fern with divided leaves arranged along a central stalk and slightly toothed leaflets.
plants.description: A perennial fern with divided leaves arranged along a central stalk. Its leaflets have slightly toothed edges and a green to brown color when dried.
medicinalUses: No well-established medicinal use specifically documented for this species.
plants.preparation: No established medicinal preparation. Primarily recognized as a fern species.
plants.habitat: Grows in moist tropical environments, particularly in shaded areas near streams and damp forest slopes.
plants.cultivation: Prefers moist, well-drained soil, shaded areas, and a humid environment. Regular watering is recommended.
plants.precautions: Avoid using the plant medicinally without proper identification and reliable safety information.
plants.funFact: This fern belongs to a diverse group of plants that reproduce through spores instead of flowers and seeds.
